learning.name: Hack Club
learning.description: Running a high-energy hacker community where students ship wild ideas every week. Organizing workshops, running code jams, and building tools that make CS accessible to everyone—no boring lectures allowed.

learning.name: Mepham Robotics – V5RC
learning.description: Engineering competitive robots and the software that drives them. Built dashboards for match scouting, autonomous routines in Python, and a team coordination app—because spreadsheets are for people who don't know how to code.

hackathons.name: Hack Club Arcade
hackathons.description: 30-day coding marathon. Shipped browser games, generative art experiments, and an interactive dev portfolio. Pulled all-nighters, traded stickers by mail, and proved that shipping daily is the ultimate skill unlock.

hackathons.name: High Seas
hackathons.description: Built a real-time maritime tracker app with live vessel data, interactive maps, and a Flask API backend. Shipped in 48 hours with a team scattered across three time zones and a truly unhinged amount of Red Bull.

hackathons.name: HackNY Spring Fling
hackathons.description: Led a three-person team through 24 sleepless hours to build StudySync—a real-time collaboration platform for students with WebSocket chat, shared whiteboards, and file drops. Won Best Education Hack.

hackathons.name: Counterspell NYC
hackathons.description: A 12-hour game jam for high school hackers. Built a pixel-art boss-rush game in vanilla JavaScript with a live leaderboard. Learned that scope creep is real and playtesting at 4 AM is a vibe.

hackathons.name: Apocalypse Hackathon
hackathons.description: Post-apocalyptic survival sim built with React and Flask. Real-time resource management, procedurally generated maps, and a leaderboard for the last person standing. Came for the theme, stayed for the merge conflicts.
